final_diagnosis.text: Plasmodium falciparum malaria in a traveller returned from Nigeria without prophylaxis, with microangiopathic haemolysis, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury and confusion mimicking thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura

final_dx.text: Plasmodium falciparum malaria in a traveller returned from Nigeria without prophylaxis, with microangiopathic haemolysis, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury and confusion mimicking thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura

secondary_findings: Confusion and acute kidney injury meet CDC and WHO-style criteria for severe infection (impaired consciousness, renal impairment); the treating team used oral artemether-lumefantrine
Raised ADAMTS13 antibody (22 U/mL) with only mildly reduced ADAMTS13 activity (49.1%): not immune TTP
Lifelong microcytosis, proposed as homozygous alpha-plus thalassaemia (curator's judgement call, not in the article)
accepted_differential: Infective gastroenteritis (including Giardia and C. difficile)
key_discriminators: travel to Nigeria without prophylaxis (H04, H05)
P. falciparum on thick and thin films
platelets recovering with antimalarial treatment alone
treatment_given: Artemether-lumefantrine for four days, started on day 2 (Figure 2); two units of packed red cells; supportive care. No plasma exchange.
outcome: Afebrile after day 2; symptoms resolved by day 5; platelets normalised and she was discharged. At one month she was well, with haemoglobin 11.6 g/dL and haematocrit 36.7% (follow-up values kept out of play).
teaching_points: Ask every febrile patient about travel: the first emergency visit missed it
Fever in a traveller back from sub-Saharan Africa is falciparum malaria until thick and thin films say otherwise, and the films should be repeated if negative
Falciparum malaria causes a thrombotic microangiopathy with schistocytes, undetectable haptoglobin, AKI and confusion that can score high on PLASMIC
An ADAMTS13 antibody alone is not diagnostic; immune TTP needs activity below 10%
Impaired consciousness or renal impairment make falciparum infection severe: intravenous artesunate is preferred
Travellers visiting friends and relatives are the group least likely to take prophylaxis

must_do.text: Take a travel history, including antimalarial prophylaxis
Send thick and thin blood films (or a rapid antigen test) for malaria urgently
Grade severity: conscious level, blood glucose and parasite count
Start artemisinin-based treatment promptly (intravenous artesunate while confused or vomiting, or a full course of artemether-lumefantrine)
Rehydrate with intravenous fluids and monitor renal function
Monitor parasite counts and blood counts until the parasitaemia clears
Transfuse red cells when the haemoglobin falls to about 6-7 g/dL

must_not_do.text: Start plasma exchange for presumed TTP
Give high-dose steroids, rituximab or caplacizumab for presumed TTP
Send her home again, or treat as gastroenteritis with antibiotics alone, without testing for malaria
Treat falciparum infection acquired in Nigeria with chloroquine

diagnosis_rubric_anchors.4: Falciparum malaria, travel exposure not cited
